## Area × heuristic view

Ranking rule (stated once, from the synthesis): KEY NOTATION: path prefixes are abbreviated with declared tokens — O:=orchestrator/src/orchestrator/ F:=fused-memory/src/fused_memory/ S:=shared/src/shared/ D:=dashboard/src/dashboard/ E:=escalation/src/escalation/ P:=sampler/src/sampler/ L:=scripts/legibility/ X:=scripts/ — and a matrix entry omits its leading `<area>|` when it equals the cell's area; an entry carrying `alias:filed-by-anchor` keeps its own area prefix (the key is unchanged, only the cell differs). Expanding the token and re-adding the cell's area reproduces the exact canonical; a stream canonical likewise omits `<area>|` when the area is the token's own package (L:→shared, X:→repo), and keeps it otherwise. Payoff = next-change cost removed × breadth × verdict weight, applied identically to every key. Cost removed = severity on the contract §4 scale (high 3, medium 2, low 1). Breadth = 2 when the finding's statement spans two or more packages or areas (every cross-area seat finding, every repo-area key, and the area-seat keys whose measurements name sites in another package), else 1. Verdict weight: confirmed 1, weakened 0.5. Ties break cross-area seat before area seat before prior, then by key. Severities and verdicts never rest on raw line count, prose share, average complexity, coverage or test count; those figures appear only as evidence inside statements. ## Findings by area

### orchestrator

**orchestrator/merge-lane** — How I read it. I read worker.py lines 1-9970 verbatim. For 9971-22081 I read a code-only rendition (docstrings and comment-only lines stripped, every code line kept) plus verbatim stretches at 18600-18930 and the __init__ block. For gates.py I read all 1,516 code lines and the header; its docstrings were not read. I read ports.py, the package __init__ and the 14 shims in full, indexed the other lane modules, and followed seams into workflow.py, git_ops.py, verify.py, harness.py, the project yamls and the PRD only far enough to anchor claims. Prose measured by AST plus tokenize: worker.py 12,762 of 22,081 lines (57.8%), gates.py 1,751 of 3,493 (50.1%), landing_evidence.py 1,529 of 2,788 (54.8%).

Overall structure. The slice is a merge lane whose correctness machinery is real but layered by accretion:
- ItemLifecycle with its legal-edge table, PermitLedger and SpeculationController with conservation audits, a LandedOutbox write-ahead journal, and frozen value types (GateVerdict, AdvanceOutcome, ChainResult) are good mechanisms.
- They sit beside older parallel encodings that were never retired: container membership, reason-string prefixes, private GitOps side channels, snapshot-dict parsing, and the raw escalation_queue next to EscalationPort.
- The 26 prior findings still hold at this tree, except that the ItemLifecycle and LaneLifecycle findings are reduced; their residue is container-driven dispatch and a heuristic recovery tree.

Where the next change costs most:
1. Cross-file invariants that live only in prose. Three worker timing constants are 'derived' in comments from config timeouts that have since moved. The no-progress budget of 5400 s now sits below every live per-command merge-verify timeout (7200-10800 s).
2. Policy copies across the workflow/worker seam: the main-health auto-heal pipeline and its eligibility guard (4 copies).
3. One-of-many mechanisms: EscalationPort carries 1 of 17 filings; gates.py encodes 'unmeasurable' four different ways, 12 of them as the pass value.
4. Code carried for features that are off fleet-wide: about 1,450 lines of probe, deep-chain and auto-chain logic threaded through _run_inflight_verify, _finalize_inflight and _dispatch_item.

Below the top findings, the smaller seams are mostly typed. gates.py's partitions form a downward DAG, so splitting it is cheap. worker.py's non-class partitions are separable except the train core, which references SpeculativeMergeWorker, and main-health, which carries a deferred import from workflow.

**orchestrator/git-worktrees** — Read at 6551b75aba. git_ops.py (15,857 lines, 58.3% prose) holds one ~13,000-line GitOps class that every subsystem goes through. Lines 1-12,780 were read in full, prose included. The remaining ~3,000 lines (advance_main, park/index-lock, cleanup, quarantine, prune) were read as code only, with their docstrings and comments skimmed. artifacts.py and offline_lane.py were read in full.

The newest code is lean and clean: branch stacking/unstacking, _worktree_add_with_retry, the merge-marker index and the commit-effect memo. The cost of the next change sits in four places:
(1) Ownership of the warm-lane state. The pool, a private GitOps._lane_lifecycle and the Harness all write durable lane records. Harness also finishes wiring GitOps after construction by setting attributes on it.
(2) One outcome axis, "warm lane unavailable", goes through three hand-kept tables: rc to enum, enum to exception, exception to disposition.
(3) git output is parsed and its exit code checked differently at each call site. Four unified-diff parsers exist, one of them with a reproduced misparse. Nine query methods drop the exit code, so a git failure reads as an empty answer.
(4) Tests reach GitOps privates directly: 31 names at 128 sites, excluding _run. That makes any split of the class expensive.

artifacts.py is coherent apart from two read-failure contracts. offline_lane.py has three mechanisms for one variability axis (which suite to run). The index-only modules are small and have clear purposes. warm_lane_pool shadows lane_lifecycle's LaneState with an enum of the same name.

The costly layer sits on top. runner.py (2533 lines, 51% prose) holds three cell executors, two fan-out loops, the gate lifecycle, the results store and the MCP stubs. Each persisted cell is a dict[str, Any], so every consumer works out its own reading with string keys and string literals: role_under_test, invocation_error markers, cost_source, verdict states and the result filename grammar. The comments then argue at length that each copy "cannot drift", and several of those copies have already drifted (role 'implementer' is never written; the judge.py and metrics.py comments contradict each other about an import cycle). The 3118 rule that a refused invocation is not a measurement is enforced only on the architect path. The pairwise judge, the comparison assessor and the reviewer-trial matcher still turn a refusal into a scored tie or a zero. So the next change costs most when it adds a field, a cause or a scorer: the agent has to find every re-derivation by reading prose, and tests built from hand-made dicts do not catch a vocabulary the producers never write.

  - The landed-row journal reaches its readers through a class-level global. MergeProvenance._outbox is set by MergeProvenance.bind, which is called only as a side effect of SpeculativeMergeWorker.__init__, and only when the worker has a project_root.

Whether TaskWorkflow and task_ground_truth see a landed row therefore depends on whether, and in what order, a merge worker was constructed earlier in the process. Readers are workflow.py (lookup x3, consume x3) and task_ground_truth.py (lookup x1). harness.py reaches the same object by a second route as well: MergeProvenance.consume x2, plus self._merge_worker._landed_outbox x4.

When nothing is bound, lookup returns None and consume is a no-op, with no log or event. The journal-first recovery guards in _recover_if_already_merged / _recover_before_execute / _recover_before_merge then degrade to their non-journal path without saying so. The class docstring also states 'last bind wins', so a second worker in one process rebinds every reader.

The test suite compensates with an autouse conftest fixture (_isolated_merge_provenance) that rebinds a fresh outbox before every orchestrator test.

It is reachable after the spawn: open(log_path, 'wb') raises OSError (ENOSPC, EMFILE or ENOENT under the disk pressure _INFRA_ERRNOS models), as can log_fh.write or flush and proc.stdout.read. When asyncio's transport is eventually garbage-collected, BaseSubprocessTransport.close() SIGKILLs the immediate child but never its group. If the cgroup scope is in use, the systemd scope stays alive too. The leg's admission slot is released while the workload still runs. verify_cmd.py::_literal_cd_target already documents that this arm turns a spawn OSError into a red that 'reads as a subproject's own red'.

Nothing catches a wrong version: the suite patches _run_cmd 199 times, and the orphan only appears as stray cargo or pytest processes on a loaded host.

  - The merge_request MCP de-dup gate makes three control decisions from SpeculativeMergeWorker.snapshot(): reaping a stale registry slot, reaping an owned corpse worktree, and C3's REJECT vs REPLACE. snapshot() is the operator rendering, an untyped dict that also serves get_merge_queue and the dashboard, and reaches the gate as live_snapshot: Callable[[], dict].

Three hand-written readers (_inflight_entry_is_stale, _inflight_worktree_is_stale, _snapshot_verify_state) each re-validate the shape: isinstance(snap, dict), an 'entries' key, entries[i].get('request_id' | 'branch' | 'verify_started_at' | 'verify_age_secs') and snap.get('owned_merge_worktrees'). Each maps any raise or unexpected shape to 'not stale / not verifying', which means coalesce. So renaming or restructuring a rendering key silently changes gate decisions:
- Losing 'owned_merge_worktrees' brings back the owned-corpse wedge the predicate fixed: every resubmit coalesces onto a corpse until restart.
- Losing 'verify_started_at' makes C3 REPLACE an in-verify entry, the mid-verify teardown C3 exists to prevent.

Each snapshot() call also runs speculation_accounting_violations, worktree_ledger_violations (an os.scandir of worktree_base with a stat per entry) and two_layer_invariants, and the gate calls it up to 3 times per merge_request. _check_request_liveness reads snapshot()['entries'][*]['state'] the same way.

  - Many GitOps query methods throw away the git return code and hand back the empty value, so callers cannot tell 'git failed' from 'nothing changed'. get_changed_files does `_, output, _ = await _run(...)`, so a git failure reaches callers as []. Three callers read [] as a safe fact:
- workflow.py's Lever B revalidation skip: zero overlap with the plan's files can short-circuit the architect's revalidation.
- workflow.py's inter-iteration rebase path.
- suffix_graph.recompute_suffix_conflict_graph, which wraps the call in `except Exception: ... treating footprint as unknown`. That handler can never fire for a nonzero git rc, so a failed probe yields an empty conflict footprint instead of 'unknown'.
The same file has five changed-file enumerators with three error contracts. get_changed_files and get_commit_changed_files return a bare list ([] on error, the first silently). get_merge_diff_files and get_branch_changed_files return a (files, err) tuple. get_files_touched_in_branch returns [] and logs a WARNING. Similar single-call queries that drop the rc include get_changed_line_ranges (a failed diff gives {}, read as stackable), get_new_side_changed_line_ranges, get_diff_from_main/base, get_main_sha and _detect_unmerged_paths, the last of which backs commit()'s conflict guard and advance_main's unmerged_state halt.

  - git_ops.py contains four separate hand-written unified-diff parsers, and each handles the known header-ambiguity hazard differently. Under --unified=0, a content line whose text starts with '++ b/' renders as '+++ b/'; likewise '-- a/' renders as '--- a/'.
- parse_diff_line_ranges matches raw prefixes with no guard.
- parse_diff_added_line_ranges guards on the previous line.
- _anchor_diff_lines classifies by hunk state, and its docstring records the false accept this hazard caused.
- _batch_added_line_counts attributes lines by block order.
I reproduced the defect in the unguarded parser on a scratch repo. Replacing line 2 of f.txt with '++ b/zzz' and changing line 6 makes parse_diff_line_ranges return {'f.txt': [(2,2)], 'zzz': [(6,6)]}, while the guarded sibling returns {'f.txt': [(2,2),(6,6)]}. The unguarded parser feeds GitOps.get_changed_line_ranges, the old-side ranges that _select_train_members uses to decide train stackability (merge_lane/worker.py and workflow.py). That method also discards the git rc, so a failed diff parses as {}, meaning 'touches nothing'. The same pattern of output parsed at each call site repeats for 'git worktree list --porcelain' (5 hand parsers: _is_registered_worktree, _worktree_holding_branch, lane_branch_checkouts, _iter_merge_worktrees, _iter_interactive_worktrees) and 'rev-list --count' (8 int-parse sites, each choosing its own fail direction).

  - measurement — reproduced misattribution: parse_diff_line_ranges -> {'f.txt': [(2, 2)], 'zzz': [(6, 6)]}; parse_diff_added_line_ranges -> {'f.txt': [(2, 2), (6, 6)]} *(rule: both functions extracted by AST from the tree at 6551b75aba and run on `git diff <root>...br --unified=0 --no-color` of a scratch repo where f.txt line 2 becomes '++ b/zzz' and line 6 changes)*
  - measurement — hand parsers of other git output: git worktree list --porcelain: 5 sites; rev-list --count + int(): 8 sites *(rule: grep "'worktree', 'list'" and "'rev-list', '--count'" in git_ops.py)*
  - next change: Plausible change: fix or extend diff parsing, for example handle copies or mode-only changes, or make stackability rename-aware.   - mcp_call(url, method, params) takes an explicit url but honours it only when the module global _session is None. McpLifecycle.start assigns that global, and McpLifecycle.stop clears it.

Which server a call reaches, and what it costs, therefore depends on whether another module ran McpLifecycle.start earlier.

Both production callers pass their own url: Scheduler's MCP fallback with config.fused_memory.url, and agents/memory_recall with an injected memory_url. Scheduler also accepts an injected _mcp_session, so it has two session channels.

  - A verify run's context is threaded as separate keyword arguments: role: Literal['merge','task','background'], is_merge_verify: bool, allow_cold_cache: bool and a derived is_cold. Those parameters encode at least five independent facts:
1. Resource class: nice prefix, cgroup cpu weight, admission slot, env, governed exec path, module fan-out semaphore, plan derivation.
2. Worktree provenance: an ephemeral merge worktree forces is_cold=True and skips _mark_verify_warm.
3. Timeout budget: the merge cold track in _resolve_verify_timeout.
4. Verdict authority: INV-1 trivial-pass escalation, written as the conjunction `role == 'merge' and is_merge_verify` at 3 sites in run_scoped_verification.
5. Retry ownership: VerifyInfraError and xdist-crash raises are gated on `not is_merge_verify`, as a stand-in for 'my caller retries' (verify.2).

The single bool is_merge_verify carries facts 2-5. role carries fact 1 and half of fact 4. Seventeen defs take role, and five take is_merge_verify: run_verification, run_scoped_verification, _resolve_verify_timeout, verify_runner.MergeVerifySpec and merge_lane/ports.run_scoped.

The call sites use four of the six combinations:
- ('merge', True) at gates.py and verify.py;
- ('merge', False) at the main-baseline probes _whole_tree_main_baseline and _probe_modules_on_main, which take merge resources but must not take merge verdict policy;
- ('task', False);
- ('background', False).
('task', True) is reachable through the type signature but has no meaning. Which flag means what lives only in docstrings, so a caller that needs merge resources with a task verdict, or the reverse, has to know the pairing rule.

### fused-memory

**fused-memory/recon-core** — The recon core is a 6.5k-line harness plus a 5.7k-line Stage-2 module that also holds Stage 3. Measured prose share is 0.46 to 0.52 in the five READ-FULLY files: harness 1,519 comment and 1,661 docstring lines; task_knowledge_sync 1,054 and 1,823. Much of that prose answers reviewers: 226 and 233 task references, 25 and 28 'amendment', 9 and 20 'reviewer', and measured censuses such as 288/165/248 tombstone victims written into docstrings.

The 25 prior findings remain open and already cover the biggest structural costs: the duplicated S1→S2→S3 run driver, Mem0 used as a control-plane ledger, stage identity as a prompt-echoed string, and test reach into privates.

What this pass adds is a recurring pattern. Wherever a new instance of an existing policy gets added, the slice has no registry, and each instance is hand-mirrored. This holds for escalation categories (one has already drifted), journal-recomputed streak escalations (two copies, a third already planned), the heterogeneous stage_reports bag that every reader branches on, the stage payload interface that forces per-run instance stashes, and the LLM-provider string axis.

Healthy spots: _recon_finding_fingerprint is one expression shared by four consumers. is_backlog_size is the single backlog predicate. _storm_summary bridges three counters onto shared.StormCounter. _flush_cycle_summaries single-sources the order of the backstop pair. The JudgeInfraError taxonomy tells infra failure apart from a verdict. Recon-report call shapes are generated from live signatures. agent_loop.py and judge.py are well-contained apart from the provider axis.

**fused-memory/recon-sweeps-guards** — The slice is a set of LLM-finding post-processors (flag_dedup's ledger dedup/suppression plus about 12 false-positive filters), deterministic Graphiti and escalation sweeps, and citation guards. All of them sit on one recurring shape: an LLM emits free-form strings (flag_type, composite task_id, status prose), and code recovers structure from them with module-local parsers and lexicons. That makes the next change cheap to write and hard to get right. Each filter is small and fail-safe in isolation, and the newer pieces are well built: FlagTypeFamily with _TaskTextAccountingGate, consolidation_gate's frozen ClosureVerdict with coded reasons, and citation_repair's INV-2 structured refusals with compare-and-set. The cost sits in the facts they share. The status vocabulary, the composite task-id shape, flag_type matching, the Graphiti edge-sweep skeleton and the fingerprint format each have several homes, and nothing ties the copies together. Several copies are justified in comments by an import rule the package does not hold: three reconciliation modules import middleware.task_interceptor, and task_filter has always lived in reconciliation/. Prose is 41-77% of every read file (measured with AST plus tokenize). Much of it is reviewer-answering task archaeology, already a prior finding, and some has drifted from the code: the citation_verifier stat-prefix contradiction, consolidation_gate's claimed EXECUTION_CLASSES import that is now a literal, preservation_specimen_guard's 'mirroring flag_dedup's block' after that block moved to standing_decision_storm_escape, and mem0_dedup naming flag_dedup as a caller although flag_dedup no longer reads Mem0. Lead check: the codebook leads (Mem0 writes vanishing, dedup under-scoped search radius, consolidation by similarity rather than correctness) point at mem0_dedup and consolidation_auto, which were indexed only. consolidation_gate refuses only on cluster malformedness, never on content correctness, and says so explicitly as a design choice, so the third lead is by design here, not a defect I can anchor. The test_flag_dedup spy on _extract_tracked_task_terms (it counts calls to pin the discovery memo) is the same seam as the prior dedup_flags/h6 finding and is not filed separately.

**fused-memory/server-tools** — The slice is three oversized files with very different shapes. tools.py (10,561 lines, 52% prose) is one 9,386-line create_mcp_server closure registering 62 tools. Every cross-cutting boundary concern is re-decided inline in each tool body: project-scope parsing, the registry and backlog gates, read journalling, write-time control flags and error envelopes. So the next change, usually "add or alter a tool", costs reading sibling tools to learn which subset of the prologue applies, and nothing checks the choice. recon_report.py (3,932 lines, 54% prose) is dominated by ReconReportState (2,695 lines). That class keeps six run-scoped maps plus per-entry mirrors and persisted slices consistent by hand, and its fix history (46 of 121 commits are fix or amend) shows that invariant is where the next change goes wrong. main.py (2,484 lines, 39% prose) is a composition root. run_server is 826 lines, wires collaborators through about a dozen post-construction setters across two duplicated TaskInterceptor arms, and states its shutdown-budget invariant in comments and a hand-counted test that no longer match the code. Healthy parts: the pure helpers at module level in tools.py (paging, update_memory arm validation, payload truncation), the extracted consolidation retain arm, and main.py's small single-purpose builders. The prose problem is real, but the prior Comments and heuristic-14 findings already cover it, and they are not restated here.

**fused-memory/task-layer-curator** — The slice is three oversized files (7,417 / 4,228 / 4,489 lines, prose 43% / 34% / 46%) holding at least ten separable responsibilities: the interceptor carries the status FSM and journal, path-scope routing (830 lines touching only 3 instance attributes), the ticket/curator worker pipeline (2,178 lines), and done-provenance validation with its own git probes. The curator carries prompt contracts, value types, the Qdrant corpus, LLM invocation and the decision pipeline. The backend carries migrations, the metadata write policy and the store. The next change is expensive in three ways. First, task facts that should have one home are re-derived per caller. Which metadata key carries a task's files has 7 readers. The candidate-key uniqueness scope is spelled 10 times. Single versus batch curation is two parallel implementations at three layers. Second, prose and dead code that claim to be live paths mislead an agent working from a partial view: a production-dead 209-line worker path still received a hardening fix three weeks after its caller was removed, and a comment claims parsers of a details marker that do not exist. Third, wire contracts encode state in strings: a combine's file union is written into details text instead of metadata.files (141 of 352 combined rows diverge live), and resolve_ticket reports a still-pending ticket as status 'failed'. What is healthy: the backend's write-authority floors and the read connection discipline are now single-sourced (stamp_pending_since, strip_machine_authored_metadata, _write_status_and_verify, _fresh_read_conn). _TicketLifecycle replaced index-space arithmetic in the batch dispatcher. clip_for_prompt and PoolWithheld single-source prompt truncation.

**fused-memory/memory-services-clients** — The slice is three backend/service files carrying the whole fused-memory write and read path. mem0_client.py (1,590 lines) is the healthiest: one timeout choke point (_timed), one filter builder, one pager, and exhaustion postures stated as typed exceptions. Its main cost is about 52% prose. graphiti_client.py (5,476 lines) is a reasonable thin-wrapper-plus-Cypher module, and its shared constants (_PROVENANCE_RANK_CLAUSE, _UUID_MEANS_LOAD, apply_incompleteness_policy) show the SPOT discipline working. Its costs come from three places. Raw Cypher is spread across about 48 query sites (prior h9). Entity identity and edge-relocation rules are restated per Cypher literal. Tests can only reach FalkorDB through private attributes. memory_service.py (11,323 lines, complexipy total 1,062) is where the next change is most expensive. A typical edit has to understand several things together: the untyped durable-queue payload dict, the late-wired collaborator setters, the 9-pass identity-reconcile chain (prior), two Layer-1 journaling policies, and a 453-line search(). Prose is about 49% of raw lines (comment-only plus docstring lines). Much of it is task archaeology and reviewer-answering defence, which priors fk-da5b47d0493a and fk-343c4a42be6b already cover. All 17 prior findings re-verified as still present at 6551b75aba. The new findings below avoid restating them. They target the wire contract, startup ordering, test seams, journaling uniformity, the search transform, the edge-property SPOT, config re-validation and two small vocabulary issues.

**new** (49)

- **`fk-0791e9817b84`** (server-tools.1) `fused-memory/src/fused_memory/server/recon_report.py::ReconReportState` — tags `h10, h11, h8, h5, comments` — **high** ✔ confirmed — structural — disposition `open`
  - ReconReportState keeps one fact in several mutable maps and holds them consistent by hand in every mutator: which findings exist in a run and under which dedup key. The run-level maps are _state, _active, _run_sig_index, _run_finding_index, _run_desc_index and _run_cited_task_index. Each _ReportEntry adds two mirrors (_signature_to_finding, _deschash_to_finding), and _persist_run/_serialize_entry add two persisted 'slices' of the run indices. Keys are computed at registration in add_finding and cite_task, then recomputed from the finding's fields in _purge_finding to undo them. tick releases them wholesale, hydrate_from_store rebuilds them by union, and _persist_run re-derives the slices. No single register/unregister operation owns the invariant 'every index entry names a live finding owned by exactly one reachable entry'. Instead it is narrated in docstrings that cite prior breaches. _reachable_run_entries documents that before task 4653 mutations of evicted-but-indexed entries were 'silently dropped on the way to the store', and that identity-deduping let a 'stale twin' overwrite the live row. add_finding's docstring proposes a fourth index to be 'maintained alongside _run_sig_index'.
  - measurement — index writers per map: _run_sig_index 5 methods (add_finding, cite_task, _purge_finding, hydrate_from_store, tick); _run_finding_index 4; _run_desc_index 4; _run_cited_task_index 3; _state 3; _active 3; per-entry mirrors 2 each *(rule: Regex over each ReconReportState method body for subscript-assign, pop, setdefault, update, clear or del on the attribute name. Read-only references are excluded. Writes through an aliased local are undercounted.)*
  - measurement — class size: 2,695 lines; add_finding 372, cite_task 353, _purge_finding 127, hydrate_from_store 122 *(rule: AST end_lineno - lineno + 1 for the class and its methods, docstrings included.)*
  - measurement — fix/amend share of commits touching recon_report.py: 46 of 121 *(rule: git log --format=%s over the file's full history at 6551b75aba, subjects matching /^(fix|amend|hotfix)|\bfix\b/i.)*
  - measurement — task-4653 reach repairs: 3 fix commits: 'dedupe persistence reach by the store's primary key', 'the purge sweep reaches evicted entries too', '_purge_finding clears dangling superseded_by' *(rule: Subjects in the same log listing that name task 4653 and an index/reach repair.)*
  - next change: The plausible next change is a new dedup key (the per-run {task_id: flag_types} index add_finding's docstring already proposes), or a new mutator such as re-targeting a finding. To get it right the agent must know all six run maps, both per-entry mirrors and both persisted slices, plus five places to update: register in add_finding or cite_task, unregister in _purge_finding by recomputing the same key from the stored finding, release in tick, rebuild in hydrate_from_store, and slice in _persist_run. It must also respect the _reachable_run_entries reach rule. A miss surfaces only when a scenario test happens to cover an evict-then-mutate or restart-then-refile path. The three task-4653 fix commits are that pattern.
  - proposal: Extract a RunFindingIndex value that owns the key derivation and the maps. It would expose register(finding, entry), unregister(finding), release(run_id), owned_slice(entry) and from_rows(rows). ReconReportState would call only those methods, and the per-entry mirrors and persisted slices would be derived from it, not maintained alongside it.

The 7 consumers are _execute_graphiti_write, _execute_mem0_write, _execute_mem0_classify_and_add, _dual_write_callback, _refresh_summaries_callback, _report_queue_dead_letter and _decode_referents, plus durable_queue.py, which itself reads '_write_op_id' and the 'add_episode'→'uuid' identity key. The contract rests on three unstated conventions. First, executors POP 8 keys (_causation_id, _write_op_id, temporal_context, unverified_claim, uuid, referents, reference_time, plus the queue's own key reads). Callbacks then read 3 of those popped keys back (_causation_id, temporal_context, unverified_claim). That only works because DurableWriteQueue._process_item deliberately parses the JSON a SECOND time for the callback ('A FRESH parse, deliberately not `payload`: _execute_write pops journal metadata that the callbacks read back out'). Second, producers disagree on which keys exist: add_memory's Graphiti payload carries no project_id, so _refresh_summaries_callback falls back group_id→project_id→'main'. Third, the 'uuid' key is load-bearing negative space, and three docstrings plus a pop-and-warn defend its absence. No type names the 18 keys, and pyright cannot see a misspelled key.

  - update_task encodes three independent write-semantics axes in two overlapping parameters across three layers.

The axes:
(a) how metadata merges: merge / additive / replace;
(b) whether details/prompt text appends;
(c) which text columns may append at all.
The parameters are metadata_mode: str | None and append: bool | None. The bool drives both (a) and (b).

The valid combinations are policed by rejection rules rather than by the parameter shape:
- In the backend's _resolve_metadata_mode: an invalid mode string; 'merge' + append=True with metadata present; a bare append=False with metadata present.
- AppendUnsupportedFieldError for title/description/priority with append=True.

The resolution is also written twice. The orchestrator client Scheduler.update_task resolves `'additive' if append else 'merge'` itself and calls its own _reject_contradictory_metadata_mode, because it 'deliberately never forwards append on the wire'. So the same append=False means 'merge' at the orchestrator boundary but is rejected at the fused-memory boundary.

SchedulerFacade.update_task still declares only append, so 5 workflow call sites need '# type: ignore' (workflow-recovery.8). The tools.update_task docstring spends about 45 lines explaining which knob governs which column.

Across 52 production update_task calls (orchestrator 39, fused-memory 13): explicit 'merge' 22, neither keyword 19, append=True 4, 'additive' 3, 'replace' 3, pass-through 1. A contributor-facing memory records that an append=True metadata edit sent with a details append 'came back scrambled'.
  - measurement — update_task calls by write-mode keywords: 52 calls: mode='merge' 22; none 19; append=True 4; mode='additive' 3; mode='replace' 3; pass-through 1 (orchestrator 39, fused-memory 13) *(rule: AST over all non-test *.py: Calls whose func name is update_task, tabulated by the append= and metadata_mode= keyword values)*
  - measurement — mode resolvers and combination guards: 2 resolvers (Scheduler.update_task client-side, sqlite_task_backend._resolve_metadata_mode); 4 combination rejections (invalid mode, merge+append=True, bare append=False, AppendUnsupportedFieldError); 2 homes of the merge+append rule (scheduler._reject_contradictory_metadata_mode, backend) *(rule: Read scheduler.py lines 2039-2080 and 4668-4740, sqlite_task_backend.py 4062-4260)*
  - measurement — axes per parameter: append drives 2 axes (metadata merge, details/prompt append); metadata_mode drives 1; column appendability is a third axis enforced by rejection *(rule: Read the tools.update_task Args docstring and _resolve_metadata_mode precedence rules)*
  - next change: An agent adding a list-valued metadata write, or a details append from orchestrator code, has to know which layer resolves append. It also has to know that SchedulerFacade does not declare metadata_mode, and that append=True means additive metadata and details-append at the same time. A wrong combination is either rejected at runtime with TASKMASTER_TOOL_ERROR, which Scheduler.update_task turns into a False return that 15 of 16 workflow call sites discard (workflow-recovery.1), or it silently unions nested lists. No type check catches it.
  - proposal: Split the wire contract into two typed enums, metadata_mode: Literal['merge','additive','replace'] (required whenever metadata is sent) and text_mode: Literal['replace','append'] applied only to details/prompt. Resolve once in the backend, delete the client-side resolver, and widen SchedulerFacade to the same two parameters.

### shared

**shared/legibility** — The slice is a 21-module, ~18k-line pipeline (inventory -> sampling -> digest -> coder -> codebook merger -> nightly trickle / census, plus trigger, state, ledger and three probes). Layering is mostly downward: the import graph has no cycles, the check_* probes defer their nightly/census_trigger imports so a probe does not load the pipeline, and trickle_state stays stdlib-only so a bare python3 predicate can run it. The healthy parts are inventory, the codebook validator and merger (append-only enforced at merge time and again by assert_no_deletion), census_identity, census_window, session_ledger (typed StrEnums), unlanded and the trickle_state classifier. Each is small and has one job. The next-change cost is in four places. (1) Several policies have two or three hand-kept copies in sibling modules that have already drifted: the signal scorer and agent-class classifier, the codebook batch-merge loop, the scoped git commit, the census: config reader, the barren-streak escalation predicate, and the escalate_info posters (prior finding). (2) Run outcomes are spread over string statuses and booleans, so a capped night has nowhere to land. (3) The two orchestrators are very long: run_census at 765 lines and run_nightly at 454. (4) Prose takes 44-63% of the core modules, much of it incident narrative. On the leads: the verifier-sandbox leads (cand-20260722-5/18) are fixed in code (census_stage_specs pins cwd=project_root with READ_ONLY_EXPLORER). The trickle-coder re-ingestion leads are fixed at the digest layer (is_reingested_content, DIGEST_INSTRUMENT_VERSION 3-5) but not in the sampler that selects sessions (finding 1).

**shared/lib** — The slice is two very large, prose-dominated runtime modules (cli_invoke.py 4,459 lines / 57.2% prose / 240 KB, 94% of the Read tool's 256 KB cap; usage_gate.py 3,052 lines / 49.7% prose) plus a ring of mostly healthy single-purpose modules. Most of the next-change cost in the CLI-invocation path is already on the books as 24 prior findings, all still present at this tree. Those findings cover the 1,016-line cap-retry loop, outcome classification decided in several places, the cli_invoke/invocation_outcome/usage_gate import cycle, tests that drive UsageGate's private state, and the cap text scraped from CLI prose. New cost found here sits elsewhere. (1) task_metadata's submodel registry is filled by import side effects, so the same parse_metadata call returns four different verdicts depending on what the process imported. That includes fused-memory's write-enforce gate, which accepts a malformed delivered_checks blob in its own import chain. (2) The CLI result-subtype vocabulary has no owner and is spelled in 5+ modules across 3 packages; a misspelled copy has already shipped once. (3) Rationale, census figures and staging notes live in code comments, and several have gone stale: false claims that work has not landed, a caller table that misses 3 callers, and a 'SOLE' claim with two live restatements. The modules I read in full and judge healthy are proc_group, delivered_check_polarity, memory_eval_metrics, sqlite_sync_base, config_dir (apart from its sweep test seam) and capability_manifest (apart from its kind×field if-ladder). They have one purpose each, enforce their invariants at more than one point, and import only downward. delivered_check_polarity's single builder/interpreter per check kind is a good model of the parity contract. Their main cost is prose volume, not structure.

**new** (20)

- **`fk-06de98fa328b`** (spot.1) `shared/src/shared/task_claimant.py::has_live_claimant` — tags `h11, inv-5, h1, comments` — **high** ~ weakened *(weakened: git grep of HEARTBEAT_TTL / claimant_liveness_ttl_secs / stale_threshold_secs in non-test .py at 6551b75aba; opened harness.py (L313-319, L5468, L16885-16920), dashboard data/tasks.py L296-307 and L700, fused-memory live_workflow_detector.py L260-271, targeted.py L2445-2471, task_ground_truth.py L31)* — structural — disposition `open`
  - 'Is this task's claimant still alive?' is decided with two different staleness thresholds, held at 7 homes in 3 packages. The predicates are shared.task_claimant.is_stranded, is_stranded_blocked and has_live_claimant. Each takes ttl as a parameter, and shared.task_claimant defines no default.

Threshold 300 s: OrchestratorConfig.claimant_liveness_ttl_secs, documented as 'the SHARED heartbeat-staleness threshold'. It is read by:
- Scheduler._eligible_for_dispatch;
- the scheduler's stranded-blocked redispatch sweep;
- Harness's re-pend liveness predicate.

Threshold 600 s: four independent module constants and one default:
- harness._RECONCILE_HEARTBEAT_TTL, used for TaskGroundTruth's reconcile sweep;
- task_ground_truth._DEFAULT_HEARTBEAT_TTL;
- dashboard data/tasks.STRANDED_HEARTBEAT_TTL, used for the dashboard's 'stranded' flag in active_tasks and task_snapshot;

### dashboard

**dashboard** — The dashboard is a FastAPI app over about 45 data modules. data/* holds the readers and aggregators, api/* holds the extracted routers, and redux_api holds the pure shapers. Layering is mostly downward: there are no import cycles except the known memory<->mcp_fanout deferred import. Invariants that the 2026-07 to 2026-09 incidents taught are now enforced by structure in several places: Datum provenance, the budgeted per-root fan-out with rotation in active_tasks, and the clock-discipline guard test (test_clock_discipline.py) that blocks SQL-side datetime('now'). The bounded-hang machinery in mcp_fanout and TTLCache is careful.

The next-change cost sits in four places.

(1) Policies are copied rather than homed: the retention SQL, the escalation status vocabulary, the label-to-root resolution and the cross-DB merge in performance.py. One of these copies, metrics.downsample_metrics, is already broken in the field: it collapses all history older than 7 days to one row.

(2) Very high prose share: mcp_fanout is 73% prose and active_tasks 63% (docstrings plus comment-only lines). That prose is full of cross-file inventories and dated measurements, and in my sample 12 of 15 such claims have gone stale.

(3) Vocabularies owned by orchestrator and escalation are re-spelled as strings. Some of these are already reported as prior findings; escalation status is new.

(4) app.py and the probe/test seams are already covered by priors.

Healthy, checked and not reported:
- db.DbPool shutdown discipline.
- The _cutoff/window helpers. They are duplicated (4 named helpers, 14 inline), but test_clock_discipline catches the dangerous wrong version.
- memory_evals' never-raise boundary. Its internal call graph is a clean DAG.

All 26 prior findings were re-verified. 25 are still present. first_success|h9 is still present only in weakened form: the failover loop is consolidated, but per-call-site exception classification still varies.

- **`fk-8adc7ac24b5b`** (dashboard.1) `dashboard/src/dashboard/data/metrics.py::downsample_metrics` — tags `h11, tests` — **medium** ✔ confirmed — mechanical — disposition `filed:6606`
  - downsample_metrics builds its hourly partition key as `strftime('%%Y-%%m-%%dT%%H', ts)`. In one branch this is an f-string and in the other a plain literal, and neither is ever %-formatted, so SQLite receives `%%`. strftime renders `%%` as a literal '%', which makes the partition key the constant '%Y-%m-%dT%H'. Every hourly pass from loops._metrics_loop therefore keeps one row per project_id (per-project tables) or one row per table (system-wide tables) out of everything older than 7 days.   - performance.py has one axis of variation, per-runs.db versus merged across DBs, and handles it with five different mechanisms, one per metric family:
- aggregate_completion_paths sums counts and recomputes pct.
- aggregate_escalation_rates sums counts and recomputes rates.
- aggregate_loop_histograms merges bins positionally, or by label on mismatch.
- aggregate_time_centiles concatenates raw samples for exact percentiles.
- _merge_history takes the unweighted mean of per-DB percentiles and percentages.

Two failure policies sit beside these. The cards path drops partial tallies (via _drop_partial_tallies) and serves UNKNOWN. The history path swallows per-DB and discovery failures at DEBUG and serves empty series.

The per-DB functions also compute derived values that the merger throws away and recomputes: the pct field of get_completion_paths, and steward_rate and interactive_rate of get_escalation_rates. get_time_centiles has no production caller at all and duplicates aggregate_time_centiles' percentile block.

The module's cognitive maximum is aggregate_loop_histograms at 49. Most of that comes from a label-mismatch branch that production cannot reach, because the bins are literals inside get_loop_histograms. Tests reach it only by monkeypatching dashboard.data.performance.get_loop_histograms.

They use frozen value objects and closed StrEnums, and each owns its vocabulary in one place. The cost of the next change sits in four places.

  - Filing an escalation varies along four independent axes, and every filing site decides each one by hand:
1. How it dedupes.
2. Which level it is born at.
3. Whether the blocking queue I/O runs off the event loop.
4. What identity a system-level (non-task) filing uses.

The escalation package has one gated mechanism for dedup, submit_or_dedupe with a DedupeConfig. Only 13 of 112 filing functions use it. Across the 112 innermost defs that construct Escalation(...) (orchestrator 83, fused-memory 21, escalation 8, in 38 modules), the dedup choices in the same def are:
- a has_open_l1 pre-check: 33;
- a get_by_task scan: 18;
- get_by_task(level=...) with a hand-chosen level: 10;
- find_pending_l2_by_root_cause: 5;
- nothing beyond a bare submit, or the dedup happens in the caller: 36.
fused-memory adds an eighth path, middleware/_folded_escalation.file_folded_escalation (8 callers), which the reconciliation package does not use.

The level axis is fixed in a method name: EscalationQueue.has_open_l1 is hard-wired to level 1. That is why lane sites hand-roll get_by_task(level=2) (merge-lane.7). The level keyword itself is a literal at each construction site: 1 ×56, 2 ×29, default ×16, 0 ×6.

Non-task identity is a task_id string convention. There are 29 distinct dunder sentinels (e.g. '__fm_read_storm__', '__merge_request_stuck__', '__session_resume_storm__') spelled once each in 11 modules, plus hyphenated non-dunder sentinels such as 'dirty-project-root-startup'.

### sampler

**sampler** — The sampler is a small, well-layered package: __main__ (oneshot shell) -> sampler.run_tick (admission + routing) -> store.LoadSampleStore (sole owner of load-samples.db), with metrics.py as pure collectors over injected seams and shared.psi as the only out-of-package import. No cycles, no reach-back, no re-export shims, cognitive max 10; write_tick is a genuinely deep one-transaction interface. The next-change cost sits in three places. First, the collection group (psi/process/load) is the package's main axis of variation but is not a value: names, window mode, admission and degrade handling are spelled per group across metrics.py, sampler.py, __main__.py and a test helper, with four reconciler tests standing in for a single home, and the admission check is a whole-tick-fatal assert that contradicts the per-group degrade policy. Second, per-leaf metrics pack (stem, leaf) into the metric string, which every consumer re-parses, and the schema has no additive-migration step to fix that cheaply. Third, the prose (store 58%, sampler 57%, metrics 53% of non-blank lines) is dominated by measurements, several of them host counts that are already false today. The process-scan corner of metrics.py re-reads every process up to 4 times while a comment says it avoids exactly that.

That is the opposite of the policy the same code states twice. __main__.main degrades each collection group independently (3 try/except blocks, 'partial writes are better than no write'), and run_tick's docstring warns against anything that would 'silently widen what a single failure erases'. So a collection failure and a vocabulary failure are handled by two different mechanisms, which is not uniform enforcement (heuristic 10). The failure mode is recorded in a test docstring in another file (test_load_metrics.py::TestEmittedNamesAreAdmittedByRunTick: 'aborts the whole tick, and the sampler writes zero rows of any group every 5 s until someone reads the journal'). ### repo

**repo/scripts-instruments** — The instruments in scripts/ are individually careful. They are read-only by construction (connect_ro, mode=ro URIs), they refuse a partial sweep (exit 3, Enumeration.complete, coverage blocks), and the newest layers are well factored: source_measures.py is a stdlib-only measure library with one parse per file and named MetricsError failures, and suite_census_pinning and merge_lane_metrics enumerate through its workspace_domain and tracked_files as they should (the 5414 lead is verified). Two kinds of next-change cost dominate. (1) Facts and policy have no home at the scripts layer, so they get re-spelled: the runs.db path and the default project root, the capability-manifest sidecar derivation and its suffix, the routing rejection vocabulary, the unit-parity CLI skeleton, the checkout-binding sys.path bootstrap, and percentile/window helpers. The shared homes that do exist (_task_db_scan, systemd_unit_parity, audit_wiped_metadata_files as a de facto library) grew by extracting fork by fork. Each extraction left re-export shims and private-name imports behind, kept so that tests and older importers resolve. (2) A heavy prose load explains what is NOT shared and why: systemd_unit_parity 79%, render_systemd_unit 60%, _task_db_scan 57%, check_dashboard_unit_parity 53%. That prose has already drifted into contradictions. An agent changing any one instrument therefore has to read two or three sibling files plus their rationale, and in most of these cases a test does not catch a divergent copy. Healthy or low-cost, and not reported: source_measures.py (its test seams, the globals() lookup in require_complexipy and the patch of _file_complexity, record-and-delegate rather than stub; minor); scan_task_toolcall_leaks.py; the mechanics of the merge_lane_metrics ledger and comparison. check_write_triage_attach_target.py (1457 lines, cognitive 38/25) still searches every calling convention and both remedy options for an attach-target contract. That contract has since landed as write_triage_judge.parse_judge_verdict(raw, slate_ids) plus CANDIDATE_ID_KEY. The probe only guards the one-time write_triage.enabled flip, so it is noted here rather than filed. The test reach into audit_manifest_descriptor_drift._expected_meta is deliberate fault injection for an implicit model coupling. It is a mild interface smell, not a finding.

**repo/scripts-operations** — The slice is two different populations. (a) Live operational code: orchestrator-watchdog.py (102 commits, 13 fix commits, runs every 60 s on the host), dashboard-watchdog.py, the sitting/ package (fan-in 9) and sweep_toolcall_markup.py (used as a periodic check). (b) One-off or trial drivers that are rarely touched again: repair_wiped_metadata_files, migrate_metadata_modules_to_files, mint_hard_v2_fixtures, run_fable_trial_v2_campaign, run_vllm_eval, load-threshold-calibration and lms_healthcheck. For population (b) the internal logic is careful and typed: frozen NamedTuples and pydantic models, named exit codes, fail-closed allowlists. Their main cost is prose. I measured prose shares of 0.43 to 0.53, much of it dated measurements and task history that belongs in commit messages, and their next-change probability is low, so I do not file findings against their internals.

sitting/inventory.py is healthy: 10% prose, frozen dataclasses, structured item keys, shortfalls counted rather than logged. The cost in the slice is concentrated in the watchdog:
- It implements one supervision policy (enabled, grace, probe, streak/cap, lease, act) once per unit kind by copying. 1019 of its 3243 lines are eight fleet/fm sibling pairs, and dashboard-watchdog.py holds a fifth copy.
- Its prose is 62% of the file and already contradicts the code in four places.
- Its 13,123-line test file reaches 24 private names at 231 sites.
- Its liveness fleet list is hand-maintained and has already drifted from the installed units.

Two cross-script SPOT failures also cost the next change:
- The hardened fused-memory MCP client and its write-success contract live inside a finished one-off migration script, and other scripts copy it.
- The sitting gates read two human-written string protocols in free-text fields, and one of them duplicates a structured field that the server enforces.

- **`fk-06de98fa328b`** (spot.1) `shared/src/shared/task_claimant.py::has_live_claimant` — tags `h11, inv-5, h1, comments` — **high** ~ weakened *(weakened: git grep of HEARTBEAT_TTL / claimant_liveness_ttl_secs / stale_threshold_secs in non-test .py at 6551b75aba; opened harness.py (L313-319, L5468, L16885-16920), dashboard data/tasks.py L296-307 and L700, fused-memory live_workflow_detector.py L260-271, targeted.py L2445-2471, task_ground_truth.py L31)* — structural — disposition `open`
  - 'Is this task's claimant still alive?' is decided with two different staleness thresholds, held at 7 homes in 3 packages. The predicates are shared.task_claimant.is_stranded, is_stranded_blocked and has_live_claimant. Each takes ttl as a parameter, and shared.task_claimant defines no default.

Threshold 300 s: OrchestratorConfig.claimant_liveness_ttl_secs, documented as 'the SHARED heartbeat-staleness threshold'. It is read by:
- Scheduler._eligible_for_dispatch;
- the scheduler's stranded-blocked redispatch sweep;
- Harness's re-pend liveness predicate.

Threshold 600 s: four independent module constants and one default:
- harness._RECONCILE_HEARTBEAT_TTL, used for TaskGroundTruth's reconcile sweep;
- task_ground_truth._DEFAULT_HEARTBEAT_TTL;
- dashboard data/tasks.STRANDED_HEARTBEAT_TTL, used for the dashboard's 'stranded' flag in active_tasks and task_snapshot;
- fused_memory services/live_workflow_detector.DEFAULT_HEARTBEAT_TTL, used for recon targeted.py and the live-workflow detector;
- artifacts.TaskArtifacts.clear_stale_plan_lock's stale_threshold_secs=600.0.

A heartbeat aged 300-600 s therefore reads as dead to the dispatcher and re-pend, but alive to the reconcile sweep, the dashboard and reconciliation. A hot reload of the knob moves only the 300 s group.

The prose has drifted in both directions. harness.py's comment on _RECONCILE_HEARTBEAT_TTL says 'No dedicated OrchestratorConfig field exists for this yet'. The dashboard and fused-memory constants each say they mirror the orchestrator's 10-minute value.
  - measurement — homes of the claimant-liveness threshold: 7: 1 config field (300 s) + 4 module constants (600 s: harness, task_ground_truth, dashboard tasks, fused-memory live_workflow_detector) + 1 hard-coded default (clear_stale_plan_lock 600.0) + 0 in shared.task_claimant *(rule: grep of HEARTBEAT_TTL / claimant_liveness_ttl_secs / stale_threshold_secs assignments in non-test .py at 6551b75aba)*
  - measurement — predicate call sites by threshold: 300 s: 4 (scheduler x3 incl. sweep ttl binding, harness x1); 600 s: 10 (task_ground_truth 1, dashboard tasks 1 feeding active_tasks/task_snapshot 3, fused-memory targeted 1 + live_workflow_detector 5) *(rule: every non-test call of is_stranded / is_stranded_blocked / has_live_claimant, classified by the ttl argument it passes)*
  - measurement — false prose claims about the threshold's home: 1 (harness.py: 'No dedicated OrchestratorConfig field exists') *(rule: read of the comments above each constant against config.py::OrchestratorConfig.claimant_liveness_ttl_secs)*
  - measurement — test files pinning a copy: 7 (dashboard 2, fused-memory 3, orchestrator 2), none asserting cross-copy equality *(rule: git grep -l of the four constant names under tests)*
  - next change: An operator or agent tunes claimant_liveness_ttl_secs, or adds a new 'stranded?' consumer, such as a dashboard tile or a recon sweep. To get it right they must know that 4 other constants in 3 packages answer the same question with 600 s, and that one comment claims the config field does not exist. Nothing catches a wrong version: each copy is pinned only by its own package's tests, and the disagreement shows up only as a task the dashboard calls live while the scheduler re-pends it.
  - proposal: Give shared.task_claimant one DEFAULT_CLAIMANT_LIVENESS_TTL and derive the OrchestratorConfig field default from it. In orchestrator, pass the config value to every predicate call. Have dashboard and fused-memory import the shared default; they already import shared.task_claimant. Delete the four module constants and the stale comment.

- as the pydantic Field default on the model class.

- review.interval 40 vs 5;
- sandbox.enabled False vs True;
- verify_clock_stop_enabled True vs False;
- merge_verify_cold_command_timeout_secs 7200 vs None;
- routing.rules and prices.

### cross:layering

Method: I read docs/code-quality.md (Definition, h9, h13, h14), quality-findings-contract §4/§6 and the INV list. I took import_graph.json (2,054 edges, 6 reach-backs, 480 deferred, 0 cycles), but its edges do not say which kind each import is, so I rebuilt a typed edge list at tree 6551b75aba with the snapshot's own parser (scripts/quality_metrics_snapshot.py internals plus source_measures.import_statements_in_tree over workspace_domain). That gave 2,350 typed rows over 690 src modules, each marked top, deferred or typecheck; saved under cross/layering/typed_edges.json.

From it I computed:
(a) Tarjan SCCs over top-level edges alone (0), over top+deferred (6: sizes 20, 3, 3, 3, 2, 2) and over all edges including TYPE_CHECKING (9, largest 24).
(b) For every non-top edge, whether its target reaches its source through top-level imports (cycle_breaking.json: 36 edges, 28 deferred and 8 typecheck).
(c) Every exhaustive combination of 5 candidate edges, to find the minimal cuts that dissolve the 20-module orchestrator SCC (minset.py).
(d) Each first-party deferred pair classified as cycle-closing, already-loaded (target is inside the importer's own top-level closure) or other: 28 / 123 / 226 of 377.
(e) A member-level cross-package matrix and a fused-memory subpackage matrix (6 bidirectional pairs), plus a stratum-role classification of all 72 reconciliation modules.

Method: Read docs/code-quality.md (definition, h3, stances, do-not-steer), docs/quality-findings-contract.md §1-6, and the INV-4/INV-5 entries of docs/legibility/design-invariants.md. Then went through the per-area findings and seams of all 16 seats and picked out the axes that cross modules or packages. Each candidate was measured on the pinned tree 6551b75aba with AST scripts and git grep over non-test *.py.

What was computed:
(1) Escalation filings. Every innermost def that constructs Escalation(...): 112 defs in 38 modules. Each was classified by the dedup/lookup calls in the same def. Also tabulated: the level= keyword at each construction, the dunder sentinel task_id literals, EscalationQueue( constructors, and file_folded_escalation callers.
(2) Verify context. Every def in verify.py, verify_plan.py, verify_runner.py, merge_lane/ports.py and gates.py that takes role / is_merge_verify / is_cold, plus the (role, is_merge_verify) keyword combination at all 23 call sites of run_verification, run_scoped_verification, run_full_verification and _resolve_verify_timeout. Each is_merge_verify branch was read.
(3) update_task calls. All 52 repo-wide, tabulated by append=/metadata_mode=. Read both mode resolvers (Scheduler.update_task + _reject_contradictory_metadata_mode, sqlite_task_backend._resolve_metadata_mode) and the tools.update_task docstring.
(4) LLM call sites by package. Which ones go through orchestrator.routing.resolve_route; the model/provider fields in fused-memory config/schema.py; the allowlist readers.
(5) Hand-rolled consecutive-streak state. AST over self.<*streak*|*consecutive*> attributes initialised to 0 or a dict, plus Streak/Breaker classes, compared with the users of orchestrator.streaks and shared.storm_counter.
(6) The two config hot-reload engines (orchestrator config.py vs fused-memory config/reload.py), compared by AST span, git log of origin and _iter_leaves bodies.

Candidates measured and dropped:
- train-vs-solo merge: already a prior GroupMergeRequest h3 cited by the merge-lane seat.
- task_kind deterministic axis: filed as a re-observation of scheduler|h12.
- parse_metadata direction/enforce: 10 call sites, too small.
- PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST sniffing: 1 production site.
- local/remote verify host: already one Protocol (VerifyRunner, LocalRunner, RemoteRunner).
- project identity: re-observation of server-tools.2.

Intermediates are in the scratchpad cross/dimensions/ (esc_filings.txt, notes.txt).

  - Filing an escalation varies along four independent axes, and every filing site decides each one by hand:
1. How it dedupes.
2. Which level it is born at.
3. Whether the blocking queue I/O runs off the event loop.
4. What identity a system-level (non-task) filing uses.

The escalation package has one gated mechanism for dedup, submit_or_dedupe with a DedupeConfig. Only 13 of 112 filing functions use it. Across the 112 innermost defs that construct Escalation(...) (orchestrator 83, fused-memory 21, escalation 8, in 38 modules), the dedup choices in the same def are:
- a has_open_l1 pre-check: 33;
- a get_by_task scan: 18;
- get_by_task(level=...) with a hand-chosen level: 10;
- find_pending_l2_by_root_cause: 5;
- nothing beyond a bare submit, or the dedup happens in the caller: 36.
fused-memory adds an eighth path, middleware/_folded_escalation.file_folded_escalation (8 callers), which the reconciliation package does not use.

The level axis is fixed in a method name: EscalationQueue.has_open_l1 is hard-wired to level 1. That is why lane sites hand-roll get_by_task(level=2) (merge-lane.7). The level keyword itself is a literal at each construction site: 1 ×56, 2 ×29, default ×16, 0 ×6.

Non-task identity is a task_id string convention. There are 29 distinct dunder sentinels (e.g. '__fm_read_storm__', '__merge_request_stuck__', '__session_resume_storm__') spelled once each in 11 modules, plus hyphenated non-dunder sentinels such as 'dirty-project-root-startup'.

The loop-offload axis is chosen per site: 5 offloaded vs 3 on-loop emitters in fused-memory (server-tools.5); submit_or_dedupe_off_loop has 1 production caller.

17 direct EscalationQueue( constructors (fused-memory 13, orchestrator 3, escalation 1) bypass the server chokepoint where born-at-L2 stamping lives (escalation.5 seam). The per-area findings merge-lane.7 (EscalationPort), workflow-recovery.5 (17 hand-built filings), scheduler-routing-config.4 (3 mechanisms in scheduler) and recon-core.1 (recon category lists) are each one area's slice of this one axis bundle.

  - A verify run's context is threaded as separate keyword arguments: role: Literal['merge','task','background'], is_merge_verify: bool, allow_cold_cache: bool and a derived is_cold. Those parameters encode at least five independent facts:
1. Resource class: nice prefix, cgroup cpu weight, admission slot, env, governed exec path, module fan-out semaphore, plan derivation.
2. Worktree provenance: an ephemeral merge worktree forces is_cold=True and skips _mark_verify_warm.
3. Timeout budget: the merge cold track in _resolve_verify_timeout.
4. Verdict authority: INV-1 trivial-pass escalation, written as the conjunction `role == 'merge' and is_merge_verify` at 3 sites in run_scoped_verification.
5. Retry ownership: VerifyInfraError and xdist-crash raises are gated on `not is_merge_verify`, as a stand-in for 'my caller retries' (verify.2).

The single bool is_merge_verify carries facts 2-5. role carries fact 1 and half of fact 4. Seventeen defs take role, and five take is_merge_verify: run_verification, run_scoped_verification, _resolve_verify_timeout, verify_runner.MergeVerifySpec and merge_lane/ports.run_scoped.

The call sites use four of the six combinations:
- ('merge', True) at gates.py and verify.py;
- ('merge', False) at the main-baseline probes _whole_tree_main_baseline and _probe_modules_on_main, which take merge resources but must not take merge verdict policy;
- ('task', False);
- ('background', False).
('task', True) is reachable through the type signature but has no meaning. Which flag means what lives only in docstrings, so a caller that needs merge resources with a task verdict, or the reverse, has to know the pairing rule.

- **`fk-ff5234ac1013`** (dimensions.3) `fused-memory/src/fused_memory/backends/sqlite_task_backend.py::_resolve_metadata_mode` — tags `h3, h12, h11, inv-5` — **medium** ✔ confirmed — structural — disposition `open`
  - update_task encodes three independent write-semantics axes in two overlapping parameters across three layers.

The axes:
(a) how metadata merges: merge / additive / replace;
(b) whether details/prompt text appends;
(c) which text columns may append at all.
The parameters are metadata_mode: str | None and append: bool | None. The bool drives both (a) and (b).

The valid combinations are policed by rejection rules rather than by the parameter shape:
- In the backend's _resolve_metadata_mode: an invalid mode string; 'merge' + append=True with metadata present; a bare append=False with metadata present.
- AppendUnsupportedFieldError for title/description/priority with append=True.

The resolution is also written twice. The orchestrator client Scheduler.update_task resolves `'additive' if append else 'merge'` itself and calls its own _reject_contradictory_metadata_mode, because it 'deliberately never forwards append on the wire'. So the same append=False means 'merge' at the orchestrator boundary but is rejected at the fused-memory boundary.

SchedulerFacade.update_task still declares only append, so 5 workflow call sites need '# type: ignore' (workflow-recovery.8). The tools.update_task docstring spends about 45 lines explaining which knob governs which column.

Across 52 production update_task calls (orchestrator 39, fused-memory 13): explicit 'merge' 22, neither keyword 19, append=True 4, 'additive' 3, 'replace' 3, pass-through 1. A contributor-facing memory records that an append=True metadata edit sent with a details append 'came back scrambled'.
  - measurement — update_task calls by write-mode keywords: 52 calls: mode='merge' 22; none 19; append=True 4; mode='additive' 3; mode='replace' 3; pass-through 1 (orchestrator 39, fused-memory 13) *(rule: AST over all non-test *.py: Calls whose func name is update_task, tabulated by the append= and metadata_mode= keyword values)*
  - measurement — mode resolvers and combination guards: 2 resolvers (Scheduler.update_task client-side, sqlite_task_backend._resolve_metadata_mode); 4 combination rejections (invalid mode, merge+append=True, bare append=False, AppendUnsupportedFieldError); 2 homes of the merge+append rule (scheduler._reject_contradictory_metadata_mode, backend) *(rule: Read scheduler.py lines 2039-2080 and 4668-4740, sqlite_task_backend.py 4062-4260)*
  - measurement — axes per parameter: append drives 2 axes (metadata merge, details/prompt append); metadata_mode drives 1; column appendability is a third axis enforced by rejection *(rule: Read the tools.update_task Args docstring and _resolve_metadata_mode precedence rules)*
  - next change: An agent adding a list-valued metadata write, or a details append from orchestrator code, has to know which layer resolves append. It also has to know that SchedulerFacade does not declare metadata_mode, and that append=True means additive metadata and details-append at the same time. A wrong combination is either rejected at runtime with TASKMASTER_TOOL_ERROR, which Scheduler.update_task turns into a False return that 15 of 16 workflow call sites discard (workflow-recovery.1), or it silently unions nested lists. - **`fk-efae65b1f9af`** (dimensions.6) `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/config.py::diff_config` — tags `h3, h11, inv-5` — **low** ✔ confirmed — structural — disposition `open`
  - Config hot-reload is one mechanism that every service needs, and it is implemented once per service.

fused-memory/config/reload.py (2026-07-18, task 2718) is a port of orchestrator/config.py's engine (2026-07-02, task 2005); its module docstring says it 'Ports the orchestrator's proven config-hot-reload engine'. Each copy has its own ConfigDiff, _iter_leaves, diff_config, _set_leaf, apply_reload and a dotted-path RELOADABLE_FIELDS allowlist: orchestrator about 134 engine lines plus a 277-line allowlist, fused-memory about 151 plus 244.

The copies have diverged. The fused-memory port fixed the esc-2718-1 defect by deciding submodel descent from the declared annotation and iterating the union of leaf paths. The orchestrator original still descends on the runtime value and indexes fresh_leaves[path], so the first Optional submodel added to OrchestratorConfig turns a None↔populated reload into a KeyError. That is latent today because OrchestratorConfig has 0 Optional submodel fields.

Whether TaskWorkflow and task_ground_truth see a landed row therefore depends on whether, and in what order, a merge worker was constructed earlier in the process. Readers are workflow.py (lookup x3, consume x3) and task_ground_truth.py (lookup x1). harness.py reaches the same object by a second route as well: MergeProvenance.consume x2, plus self._merge_worker._landed_outbox x4.

When nothing is bound, lookup returns None and consume is a no-op, with no log or event. The journal-first recovery guards in _recover_if_already_merged / _recover_before_execute / _recover_before_merge then degrade to their non-journal path without saying so. The class docstring also states 'last bind wins', so a second worker in one process rebinds every reader.

The test suite compensates with an autouse conftest fixture (_isolated_merge_provenance) that rebinds a fresh outbox before every orchestrator test.

In each case the agent must know that the journal is visible only after a worker's constructor ran. A wrong version reads None as 'not landed' and re-plans or re-merges a task. No test notices, because the autouse fixture always binds an outbox.

- **`fk-538940c8d347`** (stateless.8) `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/mcp_lifecycle.py::mcp_call` — tags `h7, h1` — **low** ✔ confirmed — structural — disposition `open`
  - mcp_call(url, method, params) takes an explicit url but honours it only when the module global _session is None. McpLifecycle.start assigns that global, and McpLifecycle.stop clears it.

After start, every call goes to the lifecycle's session regardless of url. Before start or after stop, each call builds a fresh one-shot McpSession, running a full initialize handshake on every call with nothing closing it. Which server a call reaches, and what it costs, therefore depends on whether another module ran McpLifecycle.start earlier.

Both production callers pass their own url: Scheduler's MCP fallback with config.fused_memory.url, and agents/memory_recall with an injected memory_url. Scheduler also accepts an injected _mcp_session, so it has two session channels.

The fallback derives the base URL with url.rstrip('/mcp'). That strips characters, not a suffix, so 'http://fm.example.com/mcp' becomes 'http://fm.example.co'.
  - measurement — production callers whose url argument is ignored once the global is set: 2 (scheduler.py fallback, agents/memory_recall.py) *(rule: git grep 'mcp_call(' in */src excluding the definition; read mcp_call)*
  - measurement — session channels into the scheduler's MCP calls: 2 (injected self._mcp_session; module global mcp_lifecycle._session via mcp_call) *(rule: read scheduler.py around the mcp_call fallback)*
  - measurement — rstrip misparse: 'http://fm.example.com/mcp'.rstrip('/mcp').rstrip('/') == 'http://fm.example.co' *(rule: evaluated in python3)*
  - next change: Possible next changes: pointing a component at a different fused-memory (an external URL, a per-project server, or a test double), or adding a caller that runs before the lifecycle starts. An agent passing a new url sees it silently ignored once the lifecycle session exists. Before that point, every call silently pays a handshake. The only signal is traffic arriving at the wrong server or a connection leak.
  - proposal: Make the session an explicit collaborator. McpLifecycle hands its session to Scheduler and memory_recall at construction, just as Scheduler already accepts _mcp_session. mcp_call then becomes a pure one-shot helper that uses its url, with suffix removal via removesuffix('/mcp').

### S1 One escalation filing entry point

## Contradictions

- between harness-agents.4 (typed cascade provenance on Escalation), escalation.1 (frozen resolve/park event), dimensions.1 (FilingPolicy): Three seats propose three carriers for the same fact 'this record belongs to cascade <id>': a persisted field, a callback event, and the filing policy's sentinel identity. A persisted field and an event are not exclusive, but if both exist the harness must choose which to trust. — Posed as S2's open choice. Converges if the deferral-records PRD (plans/deferral-flip-condition-prd.md), which needs a holder/notice fact that survives restarts, is in scope: then the persisted field is required and the event carries it, and S1's FilingPolicy only names the sentinel identity.
- between merge-lane.7 (widen EscalationPort to file(record, dedupe)), scheduler-routing-config.4 (one injected scheduler escalation port), dimensions.1 (one package-level filing entry point), workflow-recovery.5 (TaskWorkflow._file_escalation): Four per-area ports versus one package-level function; built separately they would be four more copies of the dedup/level/offload decision. — Resolved in S1: the package-level filing function is the mechanism and the per-area ports (EscalationPort, the scheduler port, TaskWorkflow._file_escalation, recon's registry) are thin adapters over it that only choose a FilingPolicy. Order: S1's shared function first; the adapters are the per-area migration steps.
- between S9 (previous draft: scheduler override store exposed to fused-memory through an import), layering.4 / S19 (remove the only two fm→orchestrator imports): An fm→orchestrator import for the override schema would reintroduce the edge S19 deletes; fused-memory/pyproject.toml declares no orchestrator dependency (verified: only pytest pythonpath and pyright extraPaths reach ../orchestrator/src). — Resolved: S14 homes the override/park-eviction schema, _PRIORITY_TIERS and pin-order SQL in a stdlib shared leaf (consistent with the priority_tiers|h11 prior's own proposal and S14's project_layout); both packages import downward.

## Exonerations

Metrics flag these and the reading shows them healthy. (1) Merge-lane value types: GateVerdict, AdvanceOutcome, ChainResult, PermitLedger and SpeculationController with their conservation audits, the LandedOutbox write-ahead journal and ItemLifecycle's legal-edge table are sound AS VALUE TYPES AND MECHANISMS; the residue (container membership still operative, AdvanceOutcome's failure facts travelling via GitOps _last_*, MergeProvenance's class-level bind) is filed in S6 under itemlifecycle|h10 [w,p], _map_advance_failure|h7 and mergeprovenance|h7 — this exoneration does not close those. gates.py's partitions form a downward DAG, so its split is cheap once GateMeasurement lands. (2) escalation's small modules — pins, declared_pins, canonical, disposition, classify, merge_lane_resolution, related_pending, git_authority — are pure, frozen and own their vocabularies; the escalation prose alarm (60%) is server.py and queue.py, not these. (3) sampler: __main__ → run_tick → store is a clean DAG with cognitive max 10 and write_tick a genuinely deep one-transaction interface; its findings are vocabulary and schema homes, not structure. (4) flake_ledger.py (1,917 lines, 49% prose) is coherent: free functions, one connection per entry point, compare-and-set claims, a typed (value, error) seam; verify_cmd.py is a stdlib leaf with a clean partition and stays whole. (5) shared: proc_group, delivered_check_polarity (one builder/interpreter per check kind is the model for parity contracts), memory_eval_metrics, sqlite_sync_base, config_dir (apart from the sweep test seam) are single-purpose and import downward. (6) legibility: inventory, the codebook validator/merger (append-only enforced at merge and by assert_no_deletion), census_identity, census_window, session_ledger, unlanded and the trickle_state classifier are small and single-job; the verifier-sandbox leads (cand-20260722-5/18) are fixed in code by census_stage_specs pinning cwd with READ_ONLY_EXPLORER. (7) dashboard: db.DbPool shutdown discipline, the _cutoff/window helpers (duplicated but guarded by test_clock_discipline), memory_evals' never-raise boundary with a DAG call graph, Datum provenance and the budgeted per-root fan-out with rotation. (8) recon core: _recon_finding_fingerprint shared by four consumers, is_backlog_size, _storm_summary over shared.StormCounter, _flush_cycle_summaries single-sourcing the backstop pair, the JudgeInfraError taxonomy, recon-report call shapes generated from live signatures; agent_loop.py and judge.py are well-contained apart from the provider axis (S16). (9) task layer: write-authority floors and read-connection discipline are single-sourced (stamp_pending_since, strip_machine_authored_metadata, _write_status_and_verify, _fresh_read_conn); _TicketLifecycle replaced index arithmetic; clip_for_prompt/PoolWithheld single-source prompt truncation. (10) mem0_client.py: one timeout choke point, one filter builder, one pager, typed exhaustion exceptions; its 52% prose is the only cost. (11) graphiti_client's shared constants (_PROVENANCE_RANK_CLAUSE, _UUID_MEANS_LOAD, apply_incompleteness_policy) show SPOT working; the paged-read primitive is self-contained with downward imports. (12) scripts: source_measures.py (stdlib-only, one parse per file, named MetricsError), suite_census_pinning and merge_lane_metrics enumerate through workspace_domain/tracked_files (the 5414 lead is verified), scan_task_toolcall_leaks, sitting/inventory.py (10% prose, frozen dataclasses, counted shortfalls). (13) The whole-repo import graph has no module-level cycle, and the scheduler's tick core (W10 phase order, ModuleLockTable's one park rule, one lock-event writer) is in better shape than the open priors' headline suggests. (14) usage_gate's probe dirs are now per-(account, pid) and invocation_outcome._parse_resets_at no longer invents now+1h, narrowing two priors. (15) consolidation_gate refuses only on cluster malformedness by stated design, so the codebook's 'consolidation by similarity' lead is a design choice, not a defect anchorable here.

## Critic

Verdict: revise; synthesis revised: True. Checks that came back clean: all 25 weakened verdicts in the digest appear in the matrix with [w] (none hidden from a stream); the 9 supersedes_canonical folds are absent from the matrix; the 4 fixed priors each carry a confirmed gone_verdict (escalationqueue|h10's note hedges on 'zero scans in steady state' but the headline mechanism is gone); no unverified-fixed; no one-term-of-sum (fm-msc.4 and scripts-instruments.10 report max-and-total pairs); the comments and h14 cells are not ordered by prose share or raw lines (orchestrator h14 leads with speculativemergeworker because its prior is high, not because of 22k lines; repo comments is alphabetical on a tie). Prose shares were measured under at least four different rules across seats (raw lines vs non-blank denominators; comment-only lines vs any COMMENT token including trailing comments, per the escalation seat) and the snapshot's '47% of the domain' is a fifth — they were not used to rank, and must not be compared across seats in deliberation. The breadth rule grants 2 to 'every repo-area finding' by fiat; it does not change within-area cells but would distort any cross-area ordering built on the same score. S4's remedy pre-decides the VerifyInfraError open choice (option A) that its open_choices leave open; make the remedy say 'per the open choice'. The verdict is revise because items 1, 3, 4, 6 and 8 change rankings or streams.

- inconsistent-rule @ matrix, every [w,p] cell with a this-run prior_verdict: Re-checked priors carry the PRIOR instrument's verdict weight, not the seat's. prior_open.json: gitops.commit|h10 = weakened; the git-worktrees seat re-checked it as 'contradicted more strongly than before' yet the matrix tags [w,p] (0.5). Same for _gc_recon_markers|h9 (prior weakened-high; recon-core seat: pools, search and reaper all still present, no reduction), taskgroundtruth|h10, role_level_allowlist|h10, derive_verify_plan|h11, validate_landing_evidence|h7, taskcurator|h10, schedulerfacade|h9, tickcontext|h10, _fetch_filtered_task_tree|inv-11, _reconcile_episode_identity|h10.
